claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

1. **Do you have any children, and if so, how many?** Please provide their ages and names.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my child Alex. He's 19 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 19, the key factor is whether he is still in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they remain in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he at school, college, or undertaking an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Since Alex is 19 and studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, this would typically count as approved education.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to confirm a couple more things:

**Are you responsible for Alex - meaning does he live with you, or are you contributing at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more per week, started an apprenticeship in England, or started receiving benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't. He's just focused on his studies at the moment - no work or benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 19 years old and studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, which counts as approved education
- He is under 20 years old, which means you can continue to receive Child Benefit while he remains in approved education or training
- He lives with you in the UK, so you are responsible for him
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He hasn't started paid work for 24 hours or more per week, hasn't started an apprenticeship, and isn't receiving benefits in his own right

All the eligibility criteria are met, so you should be able to claim or continue claiming Child Benefit for Alex while he continues his A-level studies.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the Child Benefit tax calculator to work out if this applies to you.

If Alex's circumstances change (such as finishing his studies, starting substantial work, or claiming benefits), you should inform HMRC as this may affect your entitlement.
